title: External audits: at least every two years, and yearly when internal audits cannot be shown to work
audience: Cleaning managers, infection prevention staff and contract managers in SA healthcare facilities
learningOutcomes: State the minimum interval for an external cleaning audit
Name the conditions that move the external cycle to yearly
Describe what an external audit reviews

instruction.heading: The minimum cycle and who may audit
instruction.body: The standard recommends an external audit no less often than every two years. The auditor must be qualified and must work for neither the facility nor the cleaning provider. The auditor may come from the wider health service, from another facility in the same local network, or from an outside agency. The external audit reviews the facility hygiene program as a whole: the skills and knowledge of staff, all cleaning policies, the in-house audit schedule, every result and variance, and the action plans. Its scope covers the work of nurses, cleaners, contractors and facility managers.

instruction.heading: What a qualified auditor brings
instruction.body: A qualified auditor should have technical knowledge of infection control hazards and risks, familiarity with cleaning standards, and an understanding of how audits are run. Communication, cultural sensitivity, skill at settling disputes and solving problems also matter, along with planning and organising ability.

instruction.heading: When the cycle tightens
instruction.body: If the facility cannot show that its internal audit process assesses cleaning against the pass levels, or that follow-up action is taken when a level is missed, a further external review should be booked inside 12 months. If the next external audit finds the in-house process sound and follow-up actions in place, the cycle returns to the two-year interval. Otherwise the cycle stays at yearly until an effective in-house process is shown.

procedure: Confirm the date of the last external audit and the due date for the next one.
Check that internal audit results are complete and show actions.
Confirm that corrective action records exist for every missed pass level.
If a gap appears, tell the manager and plan an external audit within 12 months.
Table the results at the governance committee plus the infection prevention committee.

workedExamples.situation: A facility's last external audit was 14 months ago. Its internal audit records show three areas below their acceptable level with no corrective action recorded.
workedExamples.reasoning: The facility cannot demonstrate effective internal audit and corrective action, so the external cycle is yearly until it can. An external audit is booked inside 12 months, and the three gaps are closed before it so the next audit can show improvement.

commonErrors.error: Treating the external audit as a one-off event
commonErrors.prevention: Keep the cycle active and link it to the internal audit results.

commonErrors.error: Choosing an auditor who is employed by the cleaning contractor
commonErrors.prevention: The auditor must be independent of both the facility and the cleaning provider.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson covers audit cycles only. It does not set accreditation requirements, which should be checked against the current accreditation standards.
The two-year and yearly cycles come from a 2014 standard updated in 2017. Confirm they are current.

qualityStandard: The learner states the two-year minimum and the independence rule
The learner identifies the condition that moves the cycle to yearly
documentationEvidence: External audit schedule with the due date
Corrective action evidence presented to the external auditor
summary: An external audit is recommended at least every two years
The auditor must stand apart from both the facility and its cleaning provider
The cycle becomes yearly if internal audit and corrective action cannot be shown

knowledgeChecks.question: How often should an external cleaning audit happen at minimum?
Who may act as the external auditor?
options: A cleaner employed by the facility who knows the ward team well and works nights
A qualified auditor who works for neither the facility nor the cleaning provider
Any staff member from the same ward who has done the course and knows the ward

knowledgeChecks.question: When does the external review cadence become yearly?
options: When the facility moves to a new building and the staff have new uniforms and badges
When the facility cannot show that its in-house audit process and follow-up actions work
When staff take annual leave and the rota changes each month for the whole team and the ward
